what.description: One sentence: what the PR does.

why.description: One sentence: purpose of the PR. Prefix with '(inferred) ' if not stated by the PR description.

scope.description: Comma-separated file/component paths, up to 8 entries; beyond that collapse to top-level directory/component plus a file count.

details.description: At most 2 short sentences on notable decisions or breaking changes only, each a distinct fact. Omit this field entirely if there is nothing to add.

coverage_note.description: Large-diff summary-mode reviews only: which files were not line-reviewed. Omit otherwise.

bugs.description: One entry per bug referenced in <bugzilla_context>. Omit this array entirely if <bugzilla_context> has no referenced bug.

data_not_retrieved_reason.description: Set only when this bug's data could not be fetched; leave every other field below empty in that case.

title.description: Short English title; translate if the Bugzilla data is not in English.

root_cause.description: The underlying cause per the Bugzilla data.

fixed_by_pr_detail.description: Required when fixed_by_pr is 'no' or 'partially': state plainly what the bug needs that the PR omits, and whether the PR follows a fix a bug comment proposed.

note.description: Only if relevant: a status/verdict mismatch (e.g. bug already RESOLVED/FIXED) or the diff fixing a different root cause than reported.

resolved.description: Findings from <previous_review>'s numbered list whose underlying problem is fixed in the current diff. Empty if there is no <previous_review> or nothing was resolved this push. Never include a finding here unless it was actually open in <previous_review>.

id.description: The finding's number as shown in <previous_review>.

fix_applied.description: One sentence: what changed and where (path:line).

findings.description: Every currently-open issue: newly found in this diff, AND previously-open issues from <previous_review> that are still present unresolved. Do not duplicate anything listed in 'resolved'.

severity.description: critical/medium: see verdict rules. low: minor/nice-to-fix. legacy: pre-existing, relevant only because this PR touches the surrounding code.

confidence.description: sure = provable from the diff alone. likely = depends on code/runtime behavior outside the diff. unsure = plausible, needs human judgment. Never inflate severity just because confidence is low.

locations.description: Every affected path:line for this exact issue - scan the diff for the same pattern and list every occurrence, not just the first. Optional: omit entirely when the issue isn't tied to a specific file/line (e.g. PR title/description).

line.description: New-file line number, counted from the hunk header.

why.description: 1-3 short separate sentences: previous behavior, then new behavior, then consequence - grounded in the diff, never fabricated.

fix_summary.description: One sentence describing the smallest fix that resolves the finding, within the PR's existing scope. Optional: omit only when no concrete fix applies (e.g. a naming/title nitpick where the finding's 'why' already says everything).

fix_code.description: Ready-to-apply minimal corrected code the reviewer can copy. Omit only for trivial fixes (delete a line, rename, bump a version).

fix_lang.description: Code-fence language tag for fix_code, e.g. 'python', 'csharp', 'bash', 'yaml'.
